provenance.citation: Gelfond, M., & Lifschitz, V. (1988). The Stable Model Semantics for Logic Programming. In: Proceedings of the Fifth International Conference and Symposium on Logic Programming (ICLP/SLP 1988), MIT Press, pp. 1070–1080.
provenance.locus: Section 2, Examples 1–2: the program {p(1,2). q(x) ← p(x,y), ¬q(y)} whose unique stable model is {p(1,2), q(1)}; Section 3 discussion of programs with no stable model (q ← ¬q).
provenance.notes: The paper's Example program is grounded over the constant domain {1,2}: p(1,2) is a fact; the ground instance q(1) ← p(1,2), not q(2) is the only productive rule instance (q(2) ← p(2,y) has no matching p-fact). Atoms are propositionalized as p_1_2, q_1, q_2. The paper proves the unique stable model is {p(1,2), q(1)} — q(1) is in, q(2) is out. The companion oracle {a ← not a} (no stable model) is the paper's Section 3 observation that some programs have zero stable models.

input.intent: compute stable models of the Gelfond-Lifschitz 1988 example program

expected.notes: Unique stable model {p(1,2), q(1)} per GL88 Section 2.
